title: User-centered interior finishing material selection: An immersive virtual reality-based interactive approach
central_proposition: A novel immersive virtual reality (IVR)-based interactive approach, integrating multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) for material type selection and interactive particle swarm optimization (IPSO) for aesthetic material product selection, effectively assists users in selecting desired interior finishing materials by incorporating both visual aesthetics and conventional material performance, leading to increased user satisfaction and selection efficiency.

concept_definitions.name: User-centered design (UCD)
concept_definitions.definition: focuses on understanding and achieving end-user needs and requirements.

concept_definitions.name: Immersive virtual reality (IVR)
concept_definitions.definition: provides realistic visual experiences and immersive virtual environments (IVEs) that are adequate representations of physical environments for user experience and performance exploration.

concept_definitions.name: Material collocation
concept_definitions.definition: all interior finishing materials in one room as one study object.

concept_definitions.name: Visual harmony
concept_definitions.definition: the degree of visual harmony of material collocation calculated using the normalized dissimilarity (Hausdorff distance) between the linguistic value distribution of the material collocation being estimated and a user-desired material collocation specified in the form of images.

concept_definitions.name: Interactive Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO)
concept_definitions.definition: an interactive optimization algorithm where the material collocation preference is measured by the user score.

argument_structure: The paper argues that existing interior material selection methods are deficient in addressing subjective aesthetic preferences and effective end-user involvement. It proposes a two-step IVR-based interactive approach: first, material type selection based on quantifiable performance indicators using MCDM, and second, material product selection based on visual aesthetics using an IPSO algorithm that incorporates user preference and visual harmony. This integrated approach is designed to overcome current limitations by providing an intuitive, efficient, and user-centric design experience.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The proposed system leverages IVR to create a realistic and immersive environment, enabling users to directly experience and evaluate material optical properties and emotional responses. An objective function combines calculated visual harmony (based on linguistic value distributions of material properties like color, glossiness, and metallicness) and direct user preference scores. The IPSO algorithm iteratively optimizes material collocations by feeding back this combined aesthetic measure, along with a predictive function to reduce human interaction, guiding users towards optimal and personalized design solutions. This real-time, interactive feedback loop allows for the effective integration of subjective aesthetic criteria into the design process.

findings.antecedent: Quantifiable material performance indicators (environmental factor, cost and time factor, and operation factor)
findings.consequent: Material type selection for each interior finish
findings.mechanism: MCDM analysis calculates an overall performance score for each alternative material type, which is then presented in a radar chart to visually aid user understanding of benefits and drawbacks.
findings.source: Section 4. Material type selection: multi-criteria decision making
findings.quote: This research applies an MCDM analysis in selecting material type. Three categories of quantifiable material eva-luation criteria...
findings.empirical_support_cited: Based on review of 33 material studies and market research for indicator selection, and AHP for weights.

findings.consequent: User's visual aesthetics preference assessment for interior finishing materials
findings.mechanism: IVR provides a realistic visual experience, allowing users to visually evaluate material optical properties (color, glossiness, metallicness) and emotional responses in a clear and realistic manner, better than other advanced technologies like AR for the design stage.
findings.quote: IVE is used in the proposed method to enable users to visually evaluate material optical properties in a clear and realistic manner.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cited previous research (Luigi et al., Kuliga et al., Heydarian et al.) verifying IVEs as adequate representations for user experience.

findings.antecedent: Material collocation (all interior finishing materials in one room)
findings.mechanism: The objective function combines visual harmony (h(Xi)) and user preference (ρ(Xi)) with assigned weights (θ1, θ2), aiming to maximize overall aesthetic measures.
findings.source: Section 5. Material product selection: aesthetic evaluation of material collocation
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cited previous research [19] that human preference and visual harmony both influence aesthetics.

findings.antecedent: Linguistic value distribution of material collocation (MLD) and user-desired referenced MLD
findings.mechanism: Calculated as 1 - Normalized(Dissimilarity(MLD,MLDr)), where dissimilarity is Hausdorff Distance between MLDs. MLD is derived from exciting/calm grades based on material properties (L*, A*, B*, glossiness, metallicness) projected onto a 1D linguistic-based image scale.
findings.quote: the degree of visual harmony of a material collocation solution is calculated as the normalized dissimilarity between a linguistic value distribution...
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cited previous research [36] on pleasure-related linguistic features for visual harmony evaluation.

findings.antecedent: Homeowner's direct judgment in IVR environment
findings.consequent: Preference score (p(X)) for a material collocation solution
findings.mechanism: Users assign direct ratings (-1 for unacceptable, 0 for acceptable, 1 for like) to IVR-rendered solutions, as preference is subjective and difficult to express parametrically.
findings.quote: The user can employ values -1, 0, and 1 to represent their various attitudes toward a material collocation solution...
findings.empirical_support_cited: Human judgment is incorporated in this research by directly scoring material collocation solutions rather than developing a mathematical equation.

findings.antecedent: Interactive Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm with user feedback and predictive function
findings.mechanism: IPSO iteratively generates new material collocation solutions, incorporates user preference and visual harmony scores as the overall objective value, and uses a distance-based predictive function to estimate user scores for unscored solutions, reducing human interaction while converging to optimal solutions.
findings.source: Section 5.3. IPSO algorithm for material product selection
findings.quote: an interactive particle swarm optimization (IPSO) algorithm is applied to solve the established optimization model.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cited previous research [37,38] on IPSO's robustness and efficiency compared to other evolutionary algorithms.

findings.antecedent: IVR-based interactive user-centered material selection approach
findings.mechanism: The approach effectively captures and incorporates end-users' subjective aesthetic preferences, leading to designs that are well-aligned with their expectations and reducing design changes.
findings.quote: the objective value... gradually approaches 0.68 over 175 optimization iterations, meaning that the user satisfaction level has increased by 0.28 (appropriately 40%).
findings.empirical_support_cited: Experiment results showed objective value (aesthetic measure) increased by 0.28 (40%) over 175 iterations, indicating increased user satisfaction.

findings.antecedent: IVR-based interactive user-centered material selection approach
findings.mechanism: The real-time interactive system expedites the decision-making process by providing immediate visual feedback and iterative optimization, reducing the time compared to industry benchmarks.
findings.quote: The average duration for the interactive material selection is found to be approximately 13 min, deemed acceptable by the participants.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Average duration for interactive material selection was approximately 13 min, which is below the industry benchmark (exceeds 1 h).

findings.antecedent: IVR-based interactive user-centered material selection approach
findings.consequent: Discovery of creative interior material design options
findings.mechanism: The system allows participants to explore innovative material collocations they might not have previously considered, inputting more diversity and innovation into the design process.
findings.quote: It also facilitates the discovery of creative interior material design options which the end-user or even the interior designer may not have come up with following traditional interior design practice.
findings.empirical_support_cited: The experimental results prove that the proposed interactive material selection method... facilitates the discovery of creative interior material design options.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: An IVR-based interactive material selection system will lead to higher user satisfaction with interior finishing material collocations compared to traditional methods.
The proposed IVR-IPSO approach will reduce the time required for interior finishing material selection compared to industry benchmarks.

The IVR-based interactive material selection system will facilitate the discovery of more diverse and innovative material collocation options not typically generated by traditional interior design practices.
bridge_warrants: The framework connects user-centered design (UCD) principles with immersive virtual reality (IVR) technology to enhance subjective aesthetic evaluation in material selection.
It integrates multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) for objective material performance with interactive optimization (IPSO) for subjective aesthetic preferences.

The approach bridges the gap between quantitative material evaluation and qualitative aesthetic preferences by formalizing aesthetic criteria and optimizing material collocations based on user feedback.
methodological_critiques: Existing approaches to interior finishing material selection are limited to quantitative indicators (e.g., energy performance, life expectancy) and overlook qualitative requirements such as visual-aesthetics preference.
There is a deficiency of studies analytically investigating personalized end-user aesthetic preferences in material selection.
Current UCD methods often involve ambiguous assessment of users' subjective experiences and lack enabling technology for effective end-user engagement in early design stages.
Traditional iterative optimization methods are tedious and time-consuming for material collocation, leading to user fatigue and inaccurate scoring.
model_structure: The proposed framework is a two-step process. Step 1: Material Type Selection, where MCDM analysis (considering environmental, cost/time, and operation factors) determines the appropriate material type for each interior finish. Step 2: Material Product Selection, an IVR-based interactive optimization process using IPSO. This step evaluates material collocations based on an objective function combining visual harmony (calculated from linguistic value distributions of material properties) and direct user preference scores, iteratively refining solutions in a real-time immersive environment until optimal aesthetic outcomes are achieved.
limitations: The predictive function used in the IPSO algorithm is distance-based and premised on the hypothesis that users have a similar degree of preference for similar material collocation solutions, which requires further study of the relationship between visual characteristics of materials and human preference.
The research shares a common limitation with other VR-related research regarding the difference between IVR and the physical environment.
The prototype system was verified and validated by graduate students and research staff members, not targeted homebuyers, which may limit generalizability.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Designing interactive systems with a primary focus on the user's needs, capabilities, and context leads to more effective, efficient, and satisfying outcomes in decision-making processes.
A strong sense of 'being there' within a virtual environment enhances the realism of simulated experiences, improving user engagement, immersion, and the ecological validity of material evaluation.

Material selection is a complex decision-making process involving multiple, often conflicting, performance indicators, requiring a structured approach to evaluate and weigh criteria for optimal choice.
